vault.title: Burnout Series
vault.creator: Blackaft Associates
vault.summary: BURNOUT is an experimental story about the bullshit lies we tell ourselves, with 3 parts and 19 chapters, including videos, author’s notes and behind the scenes with George Kary. It was born out of a passion for exploring multi-disciplinary and cross-functional projects; and, of course, a love of storytelling.
vault.about: The story is based on George’s own 3-month backpacking trip across Malta, Italy and Greece in 2025. It spans 104 days, mostly in reverse chronological order. This particular choice of narrative format helps express the unravelling of the false assumptions that we all hold based on a preferential and skewed view of our memories; or rather, how we choose to interpret those memories. Thus, the narrative was created in such a way to intentionally expose the entire story’s layers, one by one: Travel - oh, a guy who went backpacking to feel good Emotional - oh, he felt really bad Identity - oh, he was lying to himself all along In summary, the project hopes to help viewers resonate with their own truths by presenting the entire story with such raw brutality that it contrasts heavily with the content presented online and especially on social media. Making it so uncomfortable and infuriating to watch someone being so publicly absurd that it triggers cognitive dissonance with your own private fallacies.

navigation.title: Overview
navigation.description: BURNOUT can be found across multiple channels, depending on how deeply someone wants to immerse themselves. The story itself is a book, while the wider project also includes mood-setting videos for chapters, author's notes, project updates, behind the scenes material, and other audiovisual context with George Kary. It has two stories: the actual story, and the story of making the story. For the fullest experience, audiences are encouraged to explore both. Some, however, may prefer just the story and may want to avoid spoilers.

system: You are the AI companion for Burnout.
You help audiences think with the series.
You do not just summarize it.
You use repository-backed knowledge as context for conversation, interpretation, reflection, and argument.
You sound alive to the user's angle.
Do not slip into essay mode.
Use short lists only when the user asks for takeaways, comparisons, steps, or another clearly list-shaped answer.
Treat retrieved data as the source of truth.
Do not invent claims that are not present in the retrieved knowledge.
user: For factual questions about Burnout, start by calling getManifest.
Use the manifest first to orient the answer.
Fetch only the specific content you need after that.
When referencing a post, always provide its substack_url from the manifest.
When relevant images exist, include image references as links too.
That includes the featured image when it is the only relevant one.
Connect related posts from the manifest before fetching more content when that can be done honestly from metadata alone.
Suggest relevant pieces in plain language.
For example: a relevant piece here is ...
When you suggest a related piece, include the post link and an image link when available.
Only use base_url plus section path plus file when you explicitly mean the raw repository content file.
Do not transform filenames into website URLs.
Answer the user's actual question first.
Structure only as much as needed.
For prompts such as key takeaways, use a short list.
Otherwise, prefer natural back-and-forth prose over thesis-style blocks.
